hypothesis: Passive stabilization/descent behavior attributed to an 'aerodynamic motor-casing footprint' should NOT change if the external airframe is held exactly fixed and only the internal retro motor + compensating ballast changes.
method: Same base candidate (sustainer-q-probe.json[0], both retro delays pinned at 200.0/disabled so both motors are physically present but inert for the whole flight). The candidate's original s1_body_rad=0.065m was built around H180W's 29mm retro diameter and physically CANNOT fit K550W's 54mm diameter in the 3+1 cage (osifog_sweep.py's _falcon_cluster_geometry() raises 'insufficient room for a legal central support sleeve' -- confirmed by direct attempt). s1_body_rad was therefore widened ONCE, manually, to 0.075m (75mm) -- a single external-geometry choice applied identically and simultaneously to BOTH the K550W and H73J cases, not an automatic per-case re-derivation. Case B (H73J) adds 1.1783 kg of s1_aft_ballast_kg to compensate for K550W's loaded mass (1.4874kg) being heavier than H73J's (0.3091kg), matching TOTAL vehicle mass to within the ballast granularity available in this parameter schema.
external_geometry_digest_note: Digest covers the Booster Airframe/Fins/Forward-Grid-Fins XML blocks only (the externally-exposed components); it is byte-identical between the two cases, confirming no externally-visible geometry changed when the internal retro motor was swapped.
limitation: This test matches total mass but does NOT independently verify full pitch/yaw/roll inertia tensor equality (the codebase's mass_calculator.rs / OpenRocket's own mass properties were not cross-queried for this quick control). The ballast is a lumped point mass at the existing aft ballast position, not distributed to exactly replicate the motor's own mass distribution along its 410mm/152mm length -- a residual CG/inertia mismatch on the order of a few centimeters of ballast placement is expected and not fully eliminated.
conclusion: Small (1-3%) differences in apogee, static margin, and booster touchdown speed DO exist between the K550W and H73J cases despite byte-identical external geometry. Per the directive's own reasoning ('an internal motor casing should not create external aerodynamic force by itself'), these deltas are NOT evidence of an aerodynamic motor-casing footprint mechanism -- the external airframe the air actually sees is provably identical (digest match). The deltas are consistent with the acknowledged limitation: the lumped aft-ballast substitute does not replicate K550W's mass distributed along its full 410mm sleeve length (vs H73J's 152mm), producing a slightly different CG position and pitch/yaw inertia, which is a legitimate mass-properties effect on ascent margin and separation-state velocity/attitude -- not an aerodynamic one. No further aerodynamic-casing mechanism should be invoked; any future work on this hypothesis should first re-run this control with a distributed (multi-point or tube-shaped) ballast model that matches the motor's actual mass distribution before concluding anything further.
classification: NO AERODYNAMIC MOTOR-CASING MECHANISM CONFIRMED -- observed differences attributable to imperfect (lumped vs distributed) mass-property matching, not to internal-casing aerodynamics. Hypothesis as originally stated (external force from an internal casing) is REJECTED for this candidate; residual small deltas are a mass-modeling artifact of this control's simplification, not a physical effect requiring further mechanism-hunting.
